title: statespace lasso, version 1 (draft)
description: DRAFT, fixed by W0-S05. A liveness counterexample as TLC writes it with `-dumpTrace json <file>`, read as a lasso. Observed on tla2tools 1.8.0, build 2026.10.20.183001 (rev d2e1472, jar SHA-256 5bd7b64d...52b1e2): see RUN-tlc-lasso-json and docs/spikes/W0-S05.md. The file carries no schema marker, so this schema describes it as TLC writes it. It checks structure only. The rules that make a trace a lasso compare one part of the document with another, which JSON Schema cannot do, so they are applied after this schema passes (docs/spikes/W0-S05.md, 'Reading rules'). Unknown keys are rejected on purpose: a key listed nowhere here means the jar is not the pinned build, or the format moved.

action.description: The steps, in order; step p leaves the state with index p. A lasso has as many steps as states: the last one is the closing step, and its target repeats the state where the cycle starts. A finite counterexample has one step fewer.

state.description: The positions of the trace, indexes 1..n in order. The closing step's target is not listed again.

vars.description: The spec's variables in declaration order. The keys of a state's values are written in another order (the Hold spec declares st, tries and the file writes tries first), so read values by name.

stateIndex.description: A 1-based position in the trace, as in TLC's text trace (State 1, State 2, ...).

stateValues.title: LassoStateValues
stateValues.description: Variable name to the variable's TLA+ value as JSON. Integers, strings and functions over strings (as objects) appear in the traces W0-S05 recorded; other TLA+ values were not exercised.

location.title: LassoLocation
location.description: Where the action is defined in the spec. A step with no action behind it, such as a stutter from state 1, has module '--TLA+ BUILTINS--' and every position 0.

action.title: LassoAction
action.description: The label TLC puts on a step. It is a hint, not proof that the action ran: see the reading rules. `context` and `parameters` appeared together or not at all in every recorded trace, and only for a parameterized action: `parameters` names the parameters and `context` gives the values they took.

step.title: LassoStep
step.description: [source state, action, target state]. Both states are full copies of entries of `state`, except that the closing step's target repeats the state where the cycle starts.
